```{r echo=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)
library(readxl)
```

``` {r}
inverts <- read_excel(here("data", "inverts.xlsx"))

view(inverts)
names(inverts)
summary(inverts)

inverts_long <- pivot_longer(data = inverts,
                                    cols = '2016':'2018',
                             names_to = "year",
                             values_to = "sp_count")

inverts_long

class(inverts_long$year)

#Coerce "year" class to numeric
inverts_long <- inverts_long %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year))

```

```{r}
inverts_wide <- inverts_long %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = common_name,
                 values_from = sp_count)

inverts_wide
```


```{r}

inverts_wide < inverts_wide %>%
  clean_names()

names(inverts_wide)

```

``` {r}

inverts_unite <- inverts_long %>%
  unite(col = "site_year", #what to name the new united column
        c(site, year),# The columns we'll unite (site, year)
        sep = "_") # how to separate the things we're uniting
inverts_unite
```
###Task
Create a new object called 'inverts_moyr,' starting from inverts_long, that unites the month and year columns into a single column named "mo_yr", using a slash "/" as the separator. Then try updating the separator to something else! Like Hello
``` {r}
 inverts_moyr <- inverts_long %>%
  unite(col = "mo_yr", #what to name the new united column
  c(month, year),# The columns we'll unite (month, year)
  sep = "/") # how to separate the things we're uniting

inverts_moyr
```

``` {r}
#uniting more than 2 columns
inverts_triple_unite <- inverts_long %>%
  tidyr::unite(col = "year_site_name",
               c(year, site, common_name),
               sep = "-")
head(inverts_triple_unite)

```

```{r}
inverts_sep <- inverts_unite %>%
  tidyr::separate(site_year, into = c("my-site", "my_year"))

head(inverts_sep)

```

``` {r}
ca_abbr <- inverts %>%
  mutate(
    common_name = 
      str_replace(common_name,
                  pattern = "california",
                  replacement = "CA")
    
  )

```
